Vintage Art Kit — where it lives on the toolbar

Owner, verbatim: "Vintage Art Kit. where do we add these? show me on style toolbar on what we see." Two levels, both in the lower third, both drawn on your own screenshots of your Maker on cale-ice today — nothing above the toolbar is redrawn; the AFTER phones add only the rows that change and the pieces that appear. A is the whole page in one tap (Studio › Look). B is one scene (tap the countdown, then Style). Tap things: they work.

Page theme

A · The whole page — Studio › Look › Elements › Accents ◆

Where the look itself is picked. The art-kit builder (rd/vintage-art-kit) already put a Decorations On/Off switch under Elements; this turns that one row into the house dropdown — Accents ◆ ▾ · None · Vintage — whose choices are pictures, and lays the set's eight pieces under it as cards. One tap on Vintage = the whole set placed in its fixed spots (drapes + araña on the cover, posts at the countdown, spray + fan on e-gifts, garland over Reply, seal on the veil, oval at the closing). Tap a piece card to leave that piece out everywhere. Same column (events.site_decorations), one more value later when a second kit ships.

Tap Accents ◆ ▾ → None · Vintage, each with its picture. Vintage on: the cover above wears the drapes and the araña at once; the eight pieces sit under it as cards — tap one to leave it out of the whole Event Hub. ◆ = tried free here, named Decorations at ✓ Apply.

B · One scene — tap the countdown, then Style › Accents row

The Style toolbar exactly as you see it (your TITLE › Style screenshot, left): rows 1–3 the style cards, row 4 Colour · Size. On a scene, the cards take rows 1–2 (the Dress code's palette row already does this) and row 3 becomes Accents: the pieces on this scene as small cards — ✓ on, tap to remove — and ＋ Add, which opens a sheet of the set's eight pieces. A piece snaps to a fixed spot; while one is picked, Spot ▾ (Top · Left · Right · Corners) is the one dropdown. No drag, no free placement.

Style › Accents row — or accents as parts under the page's ＋?

Recommended · Style › Accents row (B) + Look › Accents ◆ (A)

  • One tap for the whole set in Look; per-scene pruning in Style, where the scene's look already lives.
  • Nothing new to learn: a dropdown, cards, ✓ — the shapes already on this toolbar.
  • A piece can never be mis-placed: Spot ▾ is four named boxes, written as piece + slot + scene.
  • FREE sees the row with ◆; PRO changes it. Off is always free.

Alternative · accents as parts via ＋ (my earlier idea)

  • Each piece becomes a part in the page's ＋ sheet, with its own Edit/Style/Animate.
  • More places to tap: eight parts × four tabs, and a part needs a position — a drag, or a Spot dropdown anyway.
  • The set loses its one switch: "Vintage on" would be eight adds; Apply names eight lines.
  • Harder than easy–medium for PRO, and FREE gets a ＋ sheet full of ◆ it cannot use.

⚠ Not yet one ruling. The sibling cover prototype committed this evening (prototypes/cover_scene_edit_animate_2026-10-16.html, corpus f484bca7) records the alternative as the owner's word — "Accents ◆ — their own parts, never in Style" (＋ › Accent ◆ · Spot ▾ · Animate ▾ · Remove) — while this brief was told the owner leans to Style. No DECISION_LOG row exists for either yet. Both agree on level A (Studio › Look › Accents ◆ ▾, None · Vintage) and on Spot ▾ as the only placement. Only B differs: a row in Style (here) or a part under ＋ (there). One word from the owner settles it; the data written is the same either way.

Recommendation: Style. The set is one decision (Look › Accents ◆, one tap, one Apply line) and a scene is one row (Style › Accents, ✓ and ＋ Add, Spot ▾ as the only choice).
Parts-via-＋ makes eight things of one thing and needs placement UI the Maker does not have; it also fights the builder's shipped shape (one switch, fixed slots).
Both levels write the same data: a placement list per scene (piece + spot + scene), so A's "Vintage" is simply the kit's default list and B edits that list.
